newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea sees risk of Pyongyang island incursion.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea sees risk of Pyongyang island incursion.

text.p: South Korea's Prime Minister Lee Soo-sung on Friday said that Pyongyang may launch a military incursion into islands near the border.

At a meeting of government ministers to discuss North Korea's latest threats over a submarine incident, Lee also called for heightened security at airports, ports, power plants and communication centres to protect against possible terrorist attacks, a statement from his office said.

"There is a possiblility of an incursion into the five northwest islands and the Demilitarized Zone," Lee said, referring to South Korean islands off the northwest coast of the Korean peninsula and a neutral buffer zone along the fortified land border.
The islands are seen as particularly vulnerable since they are situated above the 38th parallel dividing the two Koreas and are within sight of the North Korean mainland.
Lee also said security would be stepped up around foreign diplomatic missions, subways, department stores, train stations, highways and other public facilities.
"We will enhance diplomatic activities with our allies, including the United States and neighbouring countries," Lee was quoted as saying.
